title: Japanese Army numeric kana cipher, 1902-04: four domestic telegrams in a two-digit coordinate table (JACAR C09122911500, C09123116600, C09122909900, C03020059400)

system.summary: Each kana is two digits on a coordinate table: vowel row (a0 i1 u2 e3 o4, +5 voiced) then consonant column in reverse gojuon order (a9 ka8 ... wa0), n = 10.
system.notes: Kanji numerals in columns on Army telegraph forms, read right to left; cipher runs inside clear kana text except in C09122911500. A final 80 is taken as an end mark. A 1901 telegram (C09122806100) uses another method and is not part of this target.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decoded texts filed with three of the four telegrams (they are the cribs). No earlier reconstruction of the table found (contributor's PRIOR_CHECK.md, 20 Oct 2026; Cryptiana's meijiarmy.htm describes 1874 and 1894 Army coordinate ciphers in iroha order).

conditions.human_role: Contributed: Harumi-Matsuba directed the work; Claude Opus 5.5 searched JACAR, transcribed, built the table and ran the controls; Codex and Claude Sonnet made blind second transcriptions. No human checked the transcriptions. The project re-implemented the table, reran the control and checked two forms against the images.

solution.what: Contributor: JACAR catalogue searches and frame-by-frame viewing of the 1901-02 General Staff telegram files (about 420 items, 1,088 frames) and 235 items of the 1904 Army Ministry Daijiki; C09123116600 found by searching catalogue text for digit runs.
Contributor: digits of five telegrams transcribed by Claude; blind second transcriptions by Codex and Sonnet (lowest 97.2%, 100%, 84.6%, 87.5% for the four read).

Contributor: C09122909900's 12 pairs against the furigana of the outgoing draft (カイグン, エンシウ): n = 10, first digit mod 5 = vowel, >= 5 voiced, columns a9 ka8 sa7 in reverse gojuon order; table completed by the rule.
Contributor: C09122911500 35/35 against its translation (only the ba column fixed from it); C03020059400 10/12; permutation control 0/1000 (max 16 for 0110).
Contributor: C09123116600, no translation, reads ヨヨウノカンコクチズダイヨ (要用ノ韓国地図貸与), fitting the reply draft sending maps of Korea; kana-bigram control 0/1000 permuted tables at or above the reading.
Contributor: C09122806100 (1901) tried with the 1902 table, periodic additives of period 1-7, vowel-digit rules and iroha/gojuon shifts; nothing fits (the same ニ is 91 and 69).

Project: decode.py written from the stated table; the four telegrams decode as claimed (35/35, 11/12, 10/12, ヨヨウノカンコクチズダイヨ); shuffled-digit control, 1,000 tables each: max 16, 6, 6 against 35, 11, 10.

Project: JACAR PDFs fetched; every digit of frames 0110 and 0026 checked against the images. Found the contributor's data/transcription.txt and telegrams.tsv stale for 0110 (34 pairs, missing 18); the image and the form's 72-character count support READING.md's 35 pairs.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked the four ct_*.txt transcriptions; copied the readings table from NOTES.md with decode_out.txt (decode.py output) to texts/readings.md, and the coordinate table from NOTES.md to texts/key.md.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): texts/readings.md read per telegram. C09122911500 and C09123116600 read as sentences; C09122909900 is a 12-kana noun phrase confirmed by its draft (not prose); C03020059400 is a 12-kana phrase with two signs off the table whose sense is guessed (decoded, not read). Class read -> read in part; fraction_read 1.0 -> 0.671.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b24): the JACAR item C03020059400 (23 frames) fetched as one PDF through the viewer's raw/ path. Frame 0118 is the filed translation (訳文) of the telegram on frame 0119: '辛碇泊場司令部ニ要スル下士以下及器具材料ハ門司補給廠支廠長ニ交付済 ○ …ノ結了ハ支廠長ヨリ直接報告ノ筈', addressed 大臣宛 井上師団長.

The 12 cipher pairs re-read on frame 0119 at 400 dpi: columns 一七一〇三六一九〇? / 二八八八二九一七三一 / 一九七六, as transcribed; the last digit of pair 5 is unlike the 九 two rows above it (九 or a cursive 四: ア or ハ) and pair 7 is written 八八 (ゼ) where the translation's ジ needs 六八. Reading written from the translation with the cipher run aligned (texts/C03020059400_reading.md, _en.md); set read, grade B.

validation.notes: Japanese kana plaintext, no Japanese model in lang/; a shuffled-digit permutation control against the filed translations was run instead (decode.py control: max 16, 6, 6 of 1,000 against 35, 11, 10)

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The table was inferred from one telegram's digits against the furigana of its outgoing draft and then completed by its coordinate rule; the filed translations of two more telegrams and a reply draft check it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode_out.txt, digit pairs (end marks included): C09122911500 (36) and C09123116600 (13) read as sentences, 49 of 73 pairs (0.671). C09122909900 (12 pairs) is a heading-like noun phrase, not prose; C03020059400 (12) is decoded, not read. The earlier 1.0 (all 73 pairs take a value from the table) is withdrawn as a reading figure. 23 Oct 2026 (b24): C03020059400 (12 pairs) read with its filed translation (frame 0118); 61 of 73 pairs (0.836) in telegrams that read.

gaps.detail: The image shows 七; writer's or transmission error; JBIG2 scan.

gaps.item: C03020059400 pairs 5 and 7 (0 + 九-or-四 for ハ, 八八 for ジ) and three characters of the filed translation
gaps.detail: re-read on the JACAR scan of frames 0118-0119 (23 Oct 2026): the foot of column 1 is a glyph unlike the 九 above it; column 2 writes 八 twice; the translation is cramped after the ○

outcome.notes: fraction_coherent = 69 of 72 cipher pairs (end mark not counted) agree with the filed translation or give sense. The 35/35 of C09122911500 is partly circular (the table's shape was completed with it in view; one column value came from it); C09123116600 is the independent test but has only 13 pairs and two irregular spellings. AI transcriptions only. Outside the LLM paper's scope (Japanese, not European classical); contributed. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: C09122909900 not prose (a noun phrase), C03020059400 decoded, not read; class read -> read in part, fraction_read 1.0 -> 0.671 (pairs in the two telegrams that read).

credits.note: Found the numeric kana telegrams in JACAR, reconstructed the 1902-04 table, read four telegrams with controls; Claude Opus 5.5, Codex and Sonnet, no human check
The General Staff's and Army Ministry's filed translations and the furigana of the outgoing draft, used as cribs

texts.label: 27 Mar 1902, Osaka
texts.summary: Chief of Staff Ōyama in Osaka to Lt-Gen. Terauchi: until he returns to the capital, Terauchi is asked to handle the business of the General Staff (本職帰京迄本部ノ事務ハ貴官宜シク取計ハレタシ).

texts.label: 25 Jan 1904, Kokura
texts.summary: A request from Kokura to Maj.-Gen. Iguchi of the General Staff for the loan of the needed maps of Korea (要用ノ韓国地図貸与サレタシ); the reply draft in the same file sends maps of Korea.

texts.label: 28 Mar 1902, Osaka
texts.summary: Ōyama in Osaka to Maj.-Gen. Fukushima about observing the naval exercise (カイグン…エンシウケンガク).
texts.note: A twelve-kana noun phrase, カイグンエンシウケンガク "observation of the naval exercise", the enciphered words of an otherwise clear telegram; the draft's furigana give カイグン エンシウ, and pair 2 is written 17 (シ) for イ. Too short for sentences (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

texts.label: Jan 1904
texts.summary: Division commander Inoue to the War Minister, Jan 1904: the NCOs, men, equipment and materials needed by Anchorage Command Shin (辛碇泊場司令部, the enciphered words) have been handed to the head of the Moji branch supply depot, who will report completion directly. Read with the contemporary translation filed with it (frame 0118).

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b24): the item's frame 0118 is a contemporary translation (訳文) of the whole telegram, '辛碇泊場司令部ニ要スル下士以下及器具材料ハ門司補給廠支廠長ニ交付済。…ノ結了ハ支廠長ヨリ直接報告ノ筈'; the 12 enciphered pairs are the unit name, 10 of 12 under the 1902 table, digits re-read on frame 0119 (pair 5 '0' + a glyph read 九 that may be a cursive 四; pair 7 written 八八 for 六八). 2 of 12 kana of the cipher run rest on the translation against the figures (one on a look-alike 九/四). Two sentences, one hole (three cramped characters of the translation); _check_reading does not segment Japanese; by hand 2/2 sentences with at most one hole.
